system_architecture.overview: Custom Calculator Builder System (TIER 2E) enables dynamic creation of pricing calculators without code changes. Unlike hardcoded calculators (TIER 1), custom calculators are stored as JSON definitions in database and executed by universal wrapper. Supports formula-based calculations with parameter references, component reuse, and calculator-specific parameter overrides.

key_differences.hardcoded_calculators: Python classes with fixed logic. Fast but require code deploy to change. Used for standard products with stable pricing.
key_differences.custom_calculators: JSON definitions with formula steps. Flexible and user-editable. Used for specialty jobs, rush orders, non-standard substrates, custom quotes.

system_architecture.execution_engine: UniversalCalculatorExecutor uses asteval library for safe formula evaluation. Prevents code injection - no imports, no file I/O, no system calls. Supports: arithmetic (+, -, *, /, **, %), comparisons (<, >, <=, >=, ==, !=), logic (and, or, not), functions (min, max, abs, round).
system_architecture.parameter_resolution: Two-tier system: (1) Check custom_calculator_parameters for calculator-specific override, (2) Fall back to calculator_pricing_parameters for global default. All values converted to Decimal for precision.

custom_calculators.description: Main table storing calculator definitions as JSON. Each row is a complete calculator with inputs, formulas, and execution steps.

columns.calculator_id: UUID PRIMARY KEY - Unique identifier for calculator
columns.name: VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL - Calculator name for references (e.g., 'CustomVinylRushJob')
columns.description: TEXT - Detailed explanation of what calculator is for and when to use it
columns.short_description: VARCHAR(500) - Brief one-line summary for listings
columns.category: VARCHAR(100) - Grouping category (custom_quote, specialty_substrate, rush_job, large_format, etc.)
columns.tags: TEXT[] - Array of searchable tags for discovery
columns.json_definition: JSONB NOT NULL - Complete calculator configuration (inputs, steps, components). See json_definition_structure below.
columns.usage_instructions: TEXT - How to use this calculator, what inputs mean, typical use cases
columns.is_active: BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE - Whether calculator is ready for production use
columns.is_template: BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE - Whether this can be cloned as starting point
columns.based_on_calculator: VARCHAR(255) - Name of calculator this was cloned from (if any)
columns.usage_count: INTEGER DEFAULT 0 - How many times calculator has been executed
columns.avg_calculation_time_ms: NUMERIC - Average execution time for performance monitoring

indexes: idx_custom_calculators_active ON is_active WHERE is_active = TRUE
constraints: UNIQUE(name) - Calculator names must be unique
CHECK(json_definition IS NOT NULL) - Must have definition

custom_calculator_parameters.description: Tracks which pricing parameters each calculator uses. Enables impact analysis when parameters change.

columns.calculator_id: UUID REFERENCES custom_calculators(calculator_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
columns.parameter_name: VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL - Name of parameter (e.g., 'labor_rate_trade', 'gst_rate')
columns.source_table: VARCHAR(100) - Where parameter comes from ('calculator_pricing_parameters' or 'custom_calculator_parameters')
columns.formula_variable_name: VARCHAR(255) - Variable name used in formulas (e.g., 'labor_rate' in formula references 'param:labor_rate_trade')

constraints: UNIQUE(calculator_id, parameter_name) - No duplicate parameters per calculator

custom_calculator_components.description: Tracks which pre-built components each calculator uses. Enables component usage analytics and dependency tracking.

columns.calculator_id: UUID REFERENCES custom_calculators(calculator_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
columns.component_name: VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL - Name of component function (e.g., 'tiered_pricing_lookup', 'calculate_gst')
columns.component_type: VARCHAR(100) - Component category (pricing, tax, labor, material, etc.)
columns.usage_count: INTEGER DEFAULT 0 - How many times component is called in calculation steps

constraints: UNIQUE(calculator_id, component_name) - Track each component once per calculator

pricing_scenario_models.description: What-if analysis scenarios for testing pricing changes before applying them. Used for business intelligence.

columns.scenario_name: VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL - Descriptive name (e.g., '2025 Q1 Price Increase')
columns.parameter_changes: JSONB - Map of parameter_name -> new_value for testing

quote_history_archive.description: Historical record of all custom calculator executions for BI and auditing. Auto-populated when calculators run.

pricing_impact_projections.description: Per-calculator impact forecasts for parameter changes. Links scenarios to specific calculators.

columns.projected_impact: JSONB - Estimated price changes, volume impact, revenue impact

json_definition_structure.description: The json_definition column in custom_calculators table stores complete calculator configuration as JSONB.

required_fields.inputs: ARRAY - Defines user input parameters for calculator
required_fields.calculation_steps: ARRAY - Ordered sequence of formula and component executions

inputs_field_types.name: STRING - Variable name to use in formulas (e.g., 'width_mm', 'quantity')
inputs_field_types.label: STRING - User-facing label for input field
inputs_field_types.description: STRING - Help text explaining what this input is

inputs_field_types.options: ARRAY - For type='select', array of {value, label} objects

component.description: Call pre-built component function from common_components.py

formula_syntax_guide.engine: asteval - Safe Python expression evaluator (subset of Python)
formula_syntax_guide.security: Prevents code injection: No imports, no file I/O, no system calls, no exec/eval, no lambda, no class definitions

allowed_operations.comparison: < (less than), > (greater than), <= (less or equal), >= (greater or equal), == (equal), != (not equal)
allowed_operations.logical: and (logical and), or (logical or), not (logical not)
allowed_operations.functions: min(a, b, ...), max(a, b, ...), abs(x), round(x, digits)
allowed_operations.parentheses: ( ) for grouping and order of operations

variable_references.input_parameters: Direct reference by name: width_mm, height_mm, quantity
variable_references.previous_steps: Reference by variable name: area_m2 (from step that calculated it)

examples.conditional_logic: quantity * unit_price if quantity >= 100 else quantity * unit_price * 1.1

parameter_resolution_flow.description: Two-tier system for resolving pricing parameter values. Custom calculator overrides take precedence over global defaults.
resolution_algorithm: Step 1: Check custom_calculator_parameters table for calculator-specific override
Step 2: If override exists use that value
Step 3: If no override check calculator_pricing_parameters for global default
Step 4: If global default exists use that value
Step 5: If neither exists throw error (missing parameter)
Step 6: Convert all values to Decimal for precision in calculations
when_to_override: Calculator needs different pricing than standard (e.g., rush job premium)
Testing what-if scenarios without changing global parameters
Seasonal pricing adjustments for specific calculators

step_by_step_process: Step 1: Call custom_calculator_get_schema_guide() to learn system
Step 2: Call calculator_builder_start() with name, description, category
Step 3: Add user input parameters with calculator_builder_add_parameter() for each input field
Step 4: Add calculation steps with calculator_builder_set_formula() for formulas
Step 5: Add component steps with calculator_builder_add_component() for reusable logic
Step 6: Test calculator with calculator_builder_test() using sample inputs
Step 7: Review test results and adjust formulas/components if needed
Step 8: Save and activate with calculator_builder_save() when ready
Step 9: Query calculator with custom_calculator_get_detail() to verify
Step 10: Execute calculator via API or UI for production quotes
design_considerations: Start simple - test each step before adding complexity
Use components when possible - they're tested and optimized
Reference existing parameters for consistency across calculators
Add clear descriptions for each input and step
Test with edge cases: minimum values, maximum values, zero quantity
Consider adding validation rules to inputs (min, max ranges)
Use meaningful variable names that describe what they contain
Order steps logically - each step can reference previous steps only
Add usage_instructions to explain when to use this calculator
testing_best_practices: Test with minimum valid inputs first
Test with typical customer order values
Test edge cases: quantity = 1, very large quantities
Check GST calculation is correct (10% or double GST if Shopify)
Test parameter overrides if using custom values
Compare against similar hardcoded calculator for sanity check
Test execution time - should be under 100ms for simple calculators

execution_efficiency: Keep calculation_steps array minimal - each step adds overhead
Use components for complex logic - they're optimized
Avoid redundant calculations - store intermediate results in variables
Use formulas for simple arithmetic - faster than component calls
Test execution time with calculator_builder_test() - check execution_time_ms
Target under 100ms for simple calculators, under 500ms for complex
query_optimization: custom_calculators table has GIN indexes on json_definition and tags for fast search
Use custom_calculator_list() with filters instead of querying full table
Use custom_calculator_search() for text search - leverages indexes
Cache frequently used calculators in application memory
Batch calculator executions when possible for bulk quotes

common_errors.missing_parameter: Formula references param:xyz but parameter doesn't exist in calculator_pricing_parameters
common_errors.undefined_variable: Formula references previous_step but that step doesn't exist or is after current step
common_errors.type_error: Formula tries to add string and number - ensure inputs are correct type
common_errors.component_not_found: Component name doesn't match any of the 11 available components
common_errors.invalid_formula_syntax: Formula has syntax error - check parentheses, operators, function names
common_errors.division_by_zero: Formula divides by zero - add check or default value

error_prevention: Validate all parameter references exist before saving calculator
Test formulas with calculator_builder_test() before activating
Use try/except in formulas where division might be zero
Add input validation rules to prevent invalid values
Check component names against component_library list
Verify calculation step order - each step can only reference previous steps
